newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel not expected to attend govt news conference.
newsitem.headline: Waigel not expected to attend govt news conference.

text.p: The German government is expected on Wednesday to comment on recent foreign exchange developments at its regular news conference at 1230 GMT, government sources said on Wednesday.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel was expected to address cabinet on the current weakness of the mark and matters related to European economic and monetary union, but was not expected to attend the news conference, the sources said.
It was unclear whether Waigel would make any further public statements on Wednesday following his comments on Tuesday.
Any statements given at the regular news conference would be made by a government spokesman, who would recount the discussion in cabinet and relate any cabinet statements.
The news conference is held three times a week, generally on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, and is attended by a government spokesman and press officers from all of the government ministries.
The cabinet usually meets on Tuesdays. It is chaired by Chancellor Helmut Kohl and attended by his federal ministers.
During the summer parliamentary recess and on other special occasions it can meet at other times.

There is not usually a news conference following a cabinet meeting, unless the meeting happens to fall on a day when there is a regularly scheduled government news conference or the government plans a statement on a matter dicussed in cabinet.
